copy.HERO_DESCRIPTION: Wood-fired pizza. Pumpkin-lit paths. A family business with an extra place setting and a rather loose approach to the guest register. Pull over and stay a spell.
copy.HERO_FOOTNOTE: ALL APPETITES WELCOME. EVEN THE LIVING.

copy.HAUNTS_INTRO: Past the last sensible exit: a pizzeria, a pumpkin trail, and a counter full of disputed inventory. The family runs all three. The house supervises.

copy.STORY_EYEBROW: EVERY OLD HOUSE HAS A STORY
copy.STORY_LEDE: The family has been in hospitality since 1893. The house has been in an advisory capacity for rather longer.
STORY_PARAGRAPHS: In 1893, the first Appétit family opened a roadside kitchen for travelers who’d lost their way. They set one extra place at the first supper. By closing time, the chair had moved. The plate was clean. Nobody put it on the bill.

A few generations later, the oven is hotter, the guest register is thicker, and the extra plate is still house business. We added a pumpkin trail. The house requested a management title. We compromised on a portrait.
copy.STORY_SIGNOFF:
Some traditions are worth keeping alive.
Others handle that themselves.

copy.HERO_DESCRIPTION: A neighborhood pizzeria for the living, the dearly departed, and anyone who said they only wanted one slice. Our founder still checks the oven. He has been off payroll since 1913. Come for blistered crust, stay for the garlic knots, and please stop asking the portrait for a discount.

copy.STORY_CAPTION: THE ORIGINAL OWNER. THE ORIGINAL OBJECTION.

copy.STORY_HEADING:
He left the building.
The building *disagreed.*
copy.STORY_LEDE: Rest in Pizza began with a hot oven, a handwritten recipe, and a founder whose retirement arrangements proved unusually difficult.
STORY_PARAGRAPHS: In our fictional 1913, the founder opened a little pizza kitchen and promptly became indispensable. When he departed later that year, the family assumed the usual arrangements would apply. By Tuesday, the oven had been relit and someone had corrected the spelling on the specials board.

Today, the living staff make the pies, answer questions and take their breaks. The founder contributes a cold spot beside the flour sacks and a strong preference for the old mozzarella supplier. His portrait is consulted on heritage matters. Its purchasing authority remains suspended.

The garden came later, when a delivery of pumpkin plants proved difficult to return. The crypt began as lost property. Neither department has improved the filing system, but both give you something to explore while the next pie is in the oven.
copy.STORY_SIGNOFF:
A good neighborhood place stays with you.
Ours has taken that rather literally.
copy.STORY_FICTION: An invented family history from the fictional Old Dough Quarter.

copy.HERO_DESCRIPTION: An intimate chop house for people who enjoy a good steak and a lengthy explanation of the chair. Expect seared cuts, restrained candlelight, and a cellar committee whose members have technically stopped attending. Our maître d’ can find your table. Your ancestral seat is another department.
copy.HERO_FOOTNOTE: COMPOSED SERVICE. RESTLESS PORTRAITS. CLEAR MENU PRICES.

copy.STORY_CAPTION: A FAMILY SEAT. A MINOR OWNERSHIP DISPUTE.
copy.STORY_LEDE: Our invented estate has welcomed guests since 1866. Whether it has ever formally permitted them to leave is a matter for the guest register.
STORY_PARAGRAPHS: The first dining room was established for a family whose principal occupation was explaining the family. Supper became a public affair when a solicitor suggested that hospitality might be a more sustainable use of the silver. The suggestion was carried, subject to several unnecessary conditions.

The house now serves seared cuts, considered drinks and a composed evening at the table. The maître d’ manages the room. The portraits manage expectations. The cellar committee manages a collection of opinions that has survived all of its original members.

Between courses, take the terrace air or inspect the ancestral cabinet. Every object has a label. Few have paperwork. Our raven from Accounts regards the distinction as a budgeting issue and has requested that nobody describe the chandelier as an investment.
copy.STORY_SIGNOFF:
Good taste need not be inherited.
The dining room will accept an appetite.

copy.HERO_DESCRIPTION: A 21+ Halloween sports lodge serving smoked rib racks, cold drafts, and enough screens to monitor a minor apocalypse. Our adult hosts wear campy lumberjack pin-up uniforms; the ghosts wear whatever they died in. Come for the game. Stay because overtime has become a supernatural event.
copy.HERO_FOOTNOTE: 21+ ONLY. ADULT HOSTS. HALLOWEEN CAMP. KEEP IT RESPECTFUL.

The lodge. The garden.
The *unofficial trophies.*
copy.HAUNTS_INTRO: Big screens inside, pumpkin lanterns outside, and a trophy cabinet that has never survived a rules inquiry. Every part of this fictional lodge is 21+.
copy.MENU_INTRO: Smoked ribs, burgers, chicken, loaded snacks and sweet overtime. Suggestive names, clearly written ingredients, and absolutely no need to interview your server about the pun.
copy.MENU_NOTE: A vegetarian main and zero-proof drinks are on the menu. The entire lodge remains 21+.
copy.STORY_LEDE: In our fictional 1999, a former lumber yard acquired a kitchen, several screens and a very loose understanding of the end of a game.
STORY_PARAGRAPHS: The first monster playoff went into overtime. Then double overtime. Then the officials were declared missing, and someone ordered more ribs. The scoreboard has displayed a draw ever since. Management calls this consistency and refuses to refund the decorative trophy.

Today the lodge serves smoky plates, cold drinks and cheerfully overdone Halloween camp. Our adult hosts wear pin-up lumberjack uniforms, work actual shifts and deserve ordinary respect. The jokes are in the branding. The staff are not part of a contest, a prize package or your supernatural investigation.

The beer garden offers pumpkin lanterns and a skeleton willing to hear your theory about the referee. The trophy crypt offers six entirely unofficial legends. The bar offers a zero-proof option for the person who intends to leave while regulation time is still a meaningful concept.
copy.STORY_SIGNOFF:
Bring your friends. Bring your appetite.
Leave the ghosting to the actual ghosts.
